subject: Subprocessor delegation notice + emergency rollback plan (EdgeFlux relay)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@edgeflux.com>, security@edgeflux.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFlux relay subprocessor delegation — inventory + rollback ask

Hi team,

FYI — EdgeFlux is delegating a new relay subprocessor ("edge-relay-us-west") into their deployment that will touch telemetry and anonymized request metadata for routing. Liam attached the initial subprocessor manifest (see attachment) and flagged a go-live window for next week.

As this touches on telemetry routing and has cross-border export implications, can we do the following before we acknowledge the notice to the customer?

- Quick intake: Confirm whether this changes any export/residency posture for EU customers (I don't think so, but want explicit callout).
- Compliance asks: Kimberly, please confirm whether we need an addendum to the DPA or a simple notification.
- Ops asks: Ben, draft an emergency rollback runbook (24h turnaround) — include run triggers and contact on-call rotation.
- Procurement: Jordan, check whether contract amendment/DocuSign is required for subprocessor delegation.

Attachments: edgeflux_subprocessor_manifest_20270421.xlsx (received from EdgeFlux)

I'll hold off on acknowledging until we have quick answers.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Partner Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@edgeflux.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: security@edgeflux.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFlux relay subprocessor delegation — inventory + rollback ask

Hi Chloe / team,

Thanks for the ping. Confirming the delegation: edge-relay-us-west will handle the regional routing layer only (no full message bodies, only routing metadata and sampled telemetry).

Quick notes:
- Residency: all processing for the relay will occur in our us-west cluster; no EU export is planned for this subprocessor.
- Security: we use TLS + per-tenant tokenization; KMS is our in-house HSM-backed key store (we can share attestation and key rotation cadence).
- ETA: we plan to start a staged rollout on 2027-04-27 with a canary cohort (5%).

I've attached the manifest (edgeflux_subprocessor_manifest_20270421.xlsx) — it includes contact points, data types touched, and technical diagrams. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Compliance, EdgeFlux
liam.oconnor@edgeflux.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@edgeflux.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFlux relay subprocessor delegation — inventory + rollback ask

Chloe / Ben / Jordan / Liam — thanks for the details. A few clarifying items from legal/compliance: 

1) Data categories: the manifest calls telemetry and "anonymized request metadata" — can EdgeFlux confirm there is no identifier or pseudo-identifier (e.g., hashed_user_id) being forwarded? If hashed IDs are present, we need to confirm irreversible hashing and provide a cryptanalysis assessment.

2) KMS/HSM attestation: please provide the HSM vendor and the SOC2 report or equivalent attestation for the key store. If EdgeFlux will store any keys in their KMS, we need to know rotation cadence and whether Redwood's key material is used.

3) Emergency rollback triggers: propose we require at minimum the following triggers before we allow the canary: evidence of elevated error rates (>2x baseline for 3 consecutive five-minute windows), anomalous spike in cross-border transfers, or confirmed data handling deviations. Will EdgeFlux accept these as enforceable rollback triggers?

4) Documentation: please upload the runbook and canary plan to the shared drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/edgeflux-subprocessor-map).

If those are answered satisfactorily, I expect this can be treated as a notice (no DPA amendment) — but if any hashed IDs or key-storage concerns surface we may need a narrow addendum.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

If we need an addendum, we'll route DocuSign (DOCUSIGN-12345-EdgeFlux-Amendment). Liam, can you confirm whether EdgeFlux requests an amendment or is proceeding under the notice provision?

Ben — can you draft a minimal rollback runbook and on-call contact matrix (include paging escalation) and drop it in the shared drive? Kimberly's suggested rollback triggers sound reasonable — please include them.

Jordan Blake

Jordan / Kimberly / Chloe / Liam — attaching the initial rollback runbook (rollback_runbook_draft_v2.pdf). High level:

- Rollback triggers (first pass): >2x error rate for 15 min OR cross-border transfer spike (>50% above baseline) OR verified PII leakage incident.
- Steps:
  1) Immediate canary throttle (pause propagation)
  2) Roll routing rules back to previous stable relay (10-min DNS TTL)
  3) Invalidate temporary tokens and rotate per-tenant token key material (if used)
  4) Notify on-call (pager + slack) and open incident (INC-EDGE-0112)
- On-call matrix: primary ops (Ben Carter), backup (Dev Patel — dev.patel@redwood.com), SRE lead (Evelyn Hart).

Liam — can EdgeFlux confirm they can accept the triggers above and acknowledge a 24-hour notice window for post-mortem deliverables? If yes, we'll acknowledge the notice and begin canary on 2027-04-27 as planned.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Manager, Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachments: rollback_runbook_draft_v2.pdf
